checklist.feature: Three-storey brick wings enclosing an open courtyard
Tall, narrow gables on the principal frontage
Distinct roof intersections at the wing junctions
Dormers embedded in the roof slopes
Corner towers integrated with the roof and walls
Projecting surrounds and vertical articulation around the windows

defects: Broad, relatively even roof planes flatten the reference's more varied roofscape, particularly around the courtyard and wing junctions.
The cylindrical tower drums and simple conical caps read as separate ornaments rather than the more integrated, sharply profiled roof features visible in the reference.
Dormers and frontage gables have overly uniform geometry; several appear placed on top of a continuous roof rather than interrupting its planes.
Repeated flat window modules and continuous horizontal bands make the façades much more generic than the reference. The reference's melted photogrammetry is not evidence for irregular ornament.
fixes: Rebuild the roof kit with steeper, broken planes and explicit valleys and ridges at each wing junction; preserve the courtyard opening.
Replace the generic cylindrical tower modules with roof-integrated tower bases and caps matched to the visible corner profiles.
Give the principal-front gable modules taller, narrower profiles and check their positions and scale against each camera view.
Cut dormer openings into their host roof planes, with proper cheeks and flashing, and vary dormer size and type by roof edge.
Add restrained projecting window surrounds, sills and vertical façade divisions where supported by the reference, rather than repeating one flat surround everywhere.
Reduce the apparent size and regularity of the brick texture and add subtle material variation without copying capture artifacts.
keep: Recognisable three-storey courtyard-wing massing and overall footprint.
Legible window rhythm and distributed chimneys.
Clear daylight presentation and readable silhouette.
